Optima Algorithms¶

Optima is the constrained optimization layer built in PlussMa on top of the Series and autodiff runtime from PlussQit.

This split is intentional:

  • PlussQit owns Series, autodiff transforms, and backend compute

  • PlussMa owns numerical optimization logic and solver policy

  • optima(...) is the public constrained-solver entry point

Public Entry Point¶

The top-level call takes a constrained problem, a ParameterPack<Series> initial point, and an OptimaOptions value:

using namespace pluss::subsp::math::optim;

ConstrainedProblem problem;
ParameterPack<Series> x0;
OptimaOptions options;

options.algorithm = OptimaAlgorithm::SequentialQP;
const auto result = optima(problem, x0, options);

Problem Model¶

Optima works with:

  • a scalar objective

  • nonlinear equality constraints

  • nonlinear inequality constraints

  • linear equality constraints

  • linear inequality constraints

  • lower and upper bounds

The public parameter surface is always ParameterPack<Series>. Derivatives come from either:

  • autodiff callbacks over ParameterPack<Series>

  • user-supplied analytic callbacks

Autodiff/analytic are the derivative paths in Optima.

Shared Runtime Contract¶

All current backends reuse the same evaluation layer and diagnostics:

  • callback validation and shape checks

  • non-finite evaluation detection

  • best-feasible tracking

  • multiplier reporting

  • progress hooks

  • stall classification

  • scaling and normalization

  • dense and iterative linear-system policies

OptimaAlgorithm currently exposes:

  • MeritMethod (baseline penalty-method backend)

  • SequentialQP

  • WorkingSet

  • InternalProtocol

The primary constrained nonlinear programming backends are SequentialQP and InternalProtocol. This document focuses on those two:

  • Sequential QP

  • Internal Protocol

Common Outputs¶

Every optima(...) result exposes:

  • final parameters

  • final evaluation bundle

  • iteration count

  • function evaluation count

  • backend parameter

  • stationarity metric

  • exit flag

  • message

  • OptimaOutput

  • ConstraintMultipliers

  • optional best-feasible snapshot

The OptimaOutput payload is the main reporting surface:

Field

Meaning

algorithm

Backend label

iterations

Major iterations

function_evaluations

Total evaluation count

constraint_violation

Max violation at the returned point

first_order_optimality

First-order stationarity metric

step_size

Final accepted step fraction

line_search_fraction

Accepted line-search scaling

backend_parameter

Merit weight or barrier parameter

complementarity

Complementarity residual where applicable

krylov_iterations

Iterative linear-solver work

best_feasible_available

Whether a feasible checkpoint was found

returned_best_feasible

Whether the solver returned that checkpoint

best_feasible_value

Objective at the best feasible checkpoint

best_feasible_constraint_violation

Violation at the best feasible checkpoint

best_feasible_first_order_optimality

Stationarity at the best feasible checkpoint

multiplier_max_norm

Largest multiplier magnitude

active_multiplier_count

Count of active multipliers

detail_message

Expanded termination message

stall_category

Structured stall classification

stall_measure

Diagnostic measure associated with the stall

stall_reference

Reference threshold associated with the stall

Progress Hooks¶

Each backend option block accepts a progress_hook:

options.sequential_qp.progress_hook = [](const OptimaProgressSnapshot& s) {
  return false;
};

The snapshot includes:

  • stage

  • algorithm

  • params

  • evaluation

  • iteration

  • function_evaluations

  • step_size

  • backend_parameter

  • stationarity

  • complementarity

  • krylov_iterations

  • message

  • stall_category

  • stall_measure

  • stall_reference

  • best_feasible

Returning true requests an orderly stop.

reports::iter(std::ostream&, precision) and reports::iteration_only_trace(...) are convenience factories for per-iteration output.

To intercept the run after each iteration, use a custom hook and return true when you want to stop before the next iteration.

Internal Protocol Presets¶

Both presets below use OptimaAlgorithm::InternalProtocol; the robust preset just allocates more recovery budget and explicit solver defaults:

  • presets::internal_protocol()

  • presets::robust_internal_protocol()

Key robust deltas:

  • max_iterations: 160 (vs 100)

  • max_restoration_iterations: 10

  • max_restoration_line_search_iterations: 20

  • enable_restoration: true

  • enable_feasibility_phase: false

  • hessian_approximation: Bfgs

  • linear_system_solver: Auto

  • system_structure: Auto

Stall Taxonomy¶

Optima surfaces structured failure modes instead of only generic stop messages:

  • none

  • user-stop

  • invalid-callback-contract

  • nonfinite-callback-region

  • search-direction-collapse

  • boundary-limited

  • infeasible-stationary

  • complementarity-stagnation

  • feasibility-failure

  • recovery-failure

  • iteration-limit
